problem: Post-preflight HTTP could stall without a client deadline and cancellation could lose its reason. Late answer-publication failures could also override an already established or verified receive.
fix: Bound each exchange to30seconds through response parsing, preserve exact abort reasons and cleanup. Record native-open generation and ignore obsolete answer-publication receipts only for that established generation; genuine channel/auth/storage errors still fail.
design: Runtime discovery12seconds plus remote offer6seconds fits30seconds with margin. Deadline is per HTTP exchange, not room/user-confirmation lifetime. No automatic retries of ambiguous mutations.

Initial native UI probe had redundant waiting and did not explicitly fence body-response headers. Checked/current probe awaits headers for body phases; initial logs/source remain historical.

review.correctness: Absolute per-exchange timer stays active through success/error JSON parsing; abort reason wins over parse/transport wrapping. Timer/listener cleanup, pre-aborted callers,29-second success and DELETE404/keepalive tested. Native-open marker is generation-bound and reset on termination.
review.architecture: Only private HTTP wrapper and receiver publication lifecycle changed; no public method signature/schema, framing, hashing, buffering, destination locking or authentication policy change.
review.security: Native channel-open event, not a peer control string, establishes the marker. SAS/authorization checks and genuine channel/verification/storage failures are unchanged. Error response text remains diagnostics, not recovery instructions.
review.performance: One bounded timer/controller per HTTP exchange (health retains its own shorter deadline). No transfer-throughput/resource acceptance claim.
review.scope: Publication callback regressions use real browser WebRTC/OPFS with mocked rendezvous routing and a held response promise. HTTP stall probes use native fetch + controlled loopback server, not production LAN discovery.
